comment: Cool, another price hike and podcast ads still play for Premium users. Paying more to hear ads on a podcast app I never asked for is peak Spotify. I'll stay for the music but I'm not thrilled.

Apple Music is already at $10.99 with lossless and Spatial Audio included, so Spotify going to $10.99 without HiFi makes the comparison easy. Spotify Connect is the only reason I still have it and I'm not sure that's enough anymore.

A dollar more a month and the heart button is still gone. Charging more while the features I used for years are locked or removed is nickel and dime money grubbing. I'm not paying more until the basic playlist stuff works again.
Honestly the price is still absurdly low for the catalog. The question is where the extra dollar goes, because if it doesn't reach artists then nothing has changed for the people who make the music.
Another price rise and not a cent more for artists. Spotify keeps charging more while artists get fractions of a cent per stream. I already moved to Apple Music over that and this just reinforces it.
Price going up is annoying but it's not the reason I'm mad. I still can't see my hearts on album and track lists and now I'm paying more for it. Unsubscribe again if the hearts don't come back.
Price is whatever, I pay for control over what plays and Spotify still won't give me a true shuffle. Charging more while shuffle keeps replaying the same twenty songs is not a great look.
A buck or two more a month for the best subscription I pay for is fine by me. I'd rather they raise the price than make the ads worse. Still worth every penny.

Premium is still worth it for me in general, but I'm not paying more while the home screen looks like TikTok. If they revert the layout I'll stick around, otherwise I'm cancelling and maybe going to Tidal.
Not thrilled about the price but I still think Premium is worth it, especially if they add the features they keep promising. I'd pay a bit more for Spotlight and tabs actually working.
Price doesn't matter to me, the layout does. I already canceled over the redesign and I'll keep looking at Apple Music until the album tiles come back. Raising the price on this UI is a joke.

Premium is still worth it for the ad skipping in podcasts while I drive, but the home screen is getting out of hand. If navigation doesn't get better I'm going to Deezer and I'm not paying more for it.
Premium is still worth every penny to me. A little more a month for unlimited access with no ads is still reasonable, even if I wish the free tier wasn't so limited.

Still worth it for me with shared playlists and Connect, though I know Tidal gives better audio for similar money. Price going up a bit is fine as long as the app stays good, and I'm not switching over a dollar.
The student price going up is annoying, especially since the Showtime perk is already gone. Still a good deal with Hulu included, but I'm watching how much more they squeeze the student plan.
Price isn't really what I care about. I'm more annoyed that album radio is gone and artist names are on every track. Still the most feature-rich option I've tried.
A small price increase is fine for something I use every day, and I'm not going to cancel it over a dollar. The trial and renewal stuff is way more annoying than the price.
Paying more for the same 320 kbps is a hard pass for me. Tidal and Apple Music give lossless for similar money, so until Spotify adds it I'm just paying for convenience I could get elsewhere.
I'm on free anyway so this doesn't change much for me. Premium is already a stretch for choosing songs, and going up makes it harder to justify. I'll keep using the free playlists.
Premium at this price still beats what the other services offer for the library and Discover Weekly. I'm not happy about repeats in my recommendations, but I'd keep paying for it.
Price isn't my issue, I just want the old layout back. I'm staying on my old build and if they force the new layout on me I'm canceling the same day.

Another dollar for the best value I get from any subscription is fine. The free tier is useless so I'm paying either way. Would be nicer if they stopped shoving pop-ups at us, but Premium is still worth it.
The price doesn't bother me, the renewal pop-up does. I cancelled and it still shows up every time I open the app, and I'm tired of it getting in the way of pausing and skipping.
The price going up is the last straw for me if the recommendations keep getting worse. YouTube Music is a great deal with a strong app, so I'm going to start moving over there and I'm not sorry.
The family plan is still pretty cheap per person, so the increase doesn't bother me much. As long as nobody forces us onto a different plan and our playlists stay put, it's worth it.
I've already cancelled Premium over the feature changes so price is not really the point. Spotify keeps taking away playlist tools while raising prices and that's the part that gets me.

Spotify is raising prices and still has no lossless, while Apple and Amazon include it. Tidal already gives me hi-fi for similar money, so I'm going to move my listening there and keep Spotify only for Connect.
Price is not what I'm dealing with, it's the bugs after updates. Until the downloads and scrolling work properly I'm not going to feel good about paying more.
